1.explanation:
This minimal example uses Carbon’s Button, IconButton, and Menu components to recreate the split-button pattern shown in the bug images.  

1. We render a primary Button and an adjacent IconButton inside an inline-flex container.  
2. We toggle the menu’s open state when the IconButton is clicked, swapping between ChevronDown and ChevronUp.  
3. We grab the trigger’s bounding rectangle at render time to pass x/y coords into the Menu (so it attaches below the split control).  
4. Each MenuItem corresponds to one of the options from the scenario.  

When you run this component on a dark background, you should see exactly the closed/open states, alignment, and layering shown in the bug report screenshots.
1.bug_scenario:
The combo-button is a split control consisting of a primary action button (‘Button’) on the left and a dropdown toggle on the right. When you click the arrow, the menu appears below the split control, and the arrow flips from pointing down to pointing up. In our scenario you can see:  

• Closed state: the arrow points down, no menu visible.  
• Open state: the arrow points up, the dark-themed menu is rendered behind/under the split control and shows the three options (‘Second option’, ‘Third option’, ‘Fourth option’).  

In the images you’ll also notice slight misalignment and layering issues between the primary button and the dropdown, and inconsistent background colors between the menu and the split control.
